A sprinting stride with both feet off the ground, arms pumping, and hair trailing behind.
The figure sips sake from a small cup or bottle, often with flushed cheeks.
The head turns side to side in a clear gesture of refusal or disagreement.
A long exhale with closed eyes, drooping shoulders, and a small visible puff of breath.
The lips touch a cup or straw, drawing liquid in a small gentle drink.
The figure resting its weight on the buttocks with legs folded, bent, or hanging down.
Pursed lips suck noisily at noodles or a straw with the cheeks drawn in.
A thick lit cigar clenches in the teeth with heavy smoke curling around the face.
A lit cigarette dangles between the lips with a thin ribbon of smoke rising.
A long slender Japanese pipe held in the mouth or hand with thin smoke drifting.
The head jerks back with squeezed-shut eyes and an open mouth caught mid-sneeze.
Pursed lips expel a spray or droplet outward, often with an irritated or defiant expression.
The body wriggles and twists restlessly with shifting hips and an uneasy flustered expression.
The figure upright in a neutral vertical posture with feet planted on the ground.
Balanced upright on a single leg while the other bends or lifts free of the ground.
Arms reach overhead with an arched back and interlaced fingers in a full-body stretch.
The head bows over a desk or book, eyes cast down at the pages in concentration.
The figure samples food thoughtfully, often with a fingertip resting at the lips.
The figure lifts a small teacup to the lips, often with steam curling from it.
A mid-stride stance with one foot forward, arms swinging, and the body leaning into motion.
The mouth stretches wide open with squeezed eyes and a tilted-back head in tiredness.
Seats the figure astride a flying broom, legs hooked over the handle and hair and hem streaming back in the rush of air.
Stands the figure upright on a flying broom like a surfboard, knees bent and arms out for balance.
The figure travels through the air on an umbrella, gripping the handle high above the ground or seated in the upturned canopy.
Glasses held away from the face and wiped with a cloth or a shirt hem to clear smudges off the lenses.
A character groping about and squinting for missing glasses, often perched unnoticed on their own head.
The body strains against a weight or a grip, limbs tensed and the face clenched with effort.
Teeth clamped on a zipper pull, dragging someone else's zipper open without using hands.
Empty hands strum and fret an invisible guitar, the figure miming a rock performance with a rocking body and open mouth.
Both hands lift a hat, crown, or helmet onto the head, the piece caught halfway down and the arms raised to place it.
Hands grip a helmet and lift it off, hair spilling out as the face is uncovered and the helmet rises or hangs at the hip.
The figure holds steady on a narrow support or keeps an object poised upright, arms out for stability.
Moving forward on hands and knees with the body low to the ground.
Launches the body forward through the air with the arms reaching out to land on a target.
Walks along the narrow top of a wall with the arms out for balance above the drop on either side.
Wings caught mid-beat, raised or swept down with motion blur at the tips as the figure lifts off or hovers; arms can flap the same way.
A wing tip held between the teeth, whether the figure chews its own wing or nips at a companion's.
A large wing raised and arched overhead like an umbrella, sheltering the figure or a companion from rain or sun.

categories.name: Standing Poses
categories.description: Terms and phrases related to standing poses.

entries.description: An alert energized stance with weight forward on the toes, ready to move at once.
A suave stylish male stance with a hand in the pocket and a relaxed confident air.
The standing body tilts ahead from the hips, weight pressing toward the viewer.
A rigid formal stance with heels together, chest out, and arms straight against the sides.
Standing with one hand planted on the hip and the other arm free at the side.
An easy loose stance with soft knees, drooping shoulders, and a casual shift of weight.
The figure stands upright with a straight vertical posture and feet planted apart.
The body inverts in a handstand, legs in the air, weight entirely on the palms.
One knee touches the ground while the other leg bends forward with the foot planted.
The full weight balances on a single leg while the other bends or lifts.
The figure balances on the very tips of the toes with heels lifted high off the ground.
The standing spine curves backward, thrusting the chest and hips prominently forward.
One hand set on the hip with the elbow out; a relaxed or assertive standing beat.
Both hands on the hips, elbows out; squared and assertive.
A casual effortless upright stance with loose shoulders and arms hanging relaxed at the sides.
Standing with both arms folded across the chest in a confident guarded posture.
Standing with one ankle crossed over the other in a relaxed elegant lean.
The hips push backward so the buttocks jut out prominently behind the body.
The figure stands upright on a mattress, feet pressing down into the soft bedding.
The figure stands upright on the seat of a chair, lifted above the floor.
The figure stands or crouches on top of a desk, raised above the surrounding room.
The figure stands on a steep tiled roof with no railing, balanced on the slope high above the ground.
Standing in a slight squat with the knees turned outward and the hips pushed forward, often with hands behind the head.
Stands with each foot on a different level, one leg stepped up onto a higher surface.
Stands with one leg crossed over the other at the calf, knee, or thigh, weight settled on the back foot.

categories.name: Sitting Poses
categories.description: Terms and phrases related to sitting poses.

entries.description: Legs fold over each other with one thigh resting across the other while seated.
Seated on the ground with legs simply folded and crossed in front of the body.
The figure rests on both knees with the lower legs flat against the ground.
Sitting cross-legged with each foot resting on the opposite thigh and hands calm in the lap.
Sitting with both arms wrapped around the drawn-up knees, hugging them to the chest.
Kneeling formally with legs folded under the body and hands resting quietly on the thighs.
The figure rests on its buttocks with the torso upright and legs bent or extended.
The figure occupies a chair with the back straight or slouched against it.
The figure sinks into a cushioned sofa, usually leaning back with a relaxed posture.
Perched on the very edge of a seat with the body leaning slightly forward.
The figure rests directly on the bare floor with no furniture beneath.
The figure sits turned sideways with both legs angled to one side of the body.
Seated with the knees pushed far apart, exposing the space between the thighs.
The body lowers onto bent legs with heels down and knees spread wide apart.
Sitting with the soles together; usually lands as cross-legged and may add a butterfly.
The formal kneeling bow with hands together, more exact than prostration.
Sitting with one ankle on the other knee; on illustrious-family models it produced a seated figurine instead.
Seated or bent with both hands resting on the knees.
Seated with knees pulled up to the chest and arms wrapped tightly around them.
Sitting cross-legged.
Both knees on the ground, torso upright.
Both knees drawn up, sitting hugging the knees; hug own knees or knees to chest is more reliable, and knee up raises one.
The kneeling bow without clothes; folded cloth for clothes set beside.
One knee rests on the ground while the other foot plants forward in a proposal pose.
Kneeling bowed to the ground toward the viewer, face usually hidden; reliable.
Seated on the mattress, usually on the edge with the feet on the floor.
Seated on a bench, outdoors or in a corridor.
Seated on a chair with the back and seat visible.
Seated directly on the floor or ground.
Seated on a sofa or couch, often sunk into the cushions.
A seated split; side sitting split and front sitting split both tend to raise one leg, so add stretching and spread legs.
Seated with both legs extended straight forward and heels resting on the ground.
The thighs actively part and open wide while seated, deliberately exposing the groin.
The three-point hero landing; the pose does not come and the subject turns into a suited superhero.
Kneeling with the legs folded outward to either side and the buttocks resting between the heels.
Sits on the floor with one leg extended and bends sideways to reach the outstretched foot with one or both hands.
Sits on the floor with the knees together and both lower legs folded out to one side in a demure posture.

categories.name: Reclining and Lying Poses
categories.description: Terms and phrases related to reclining and lying poses.

entries.description: A hand clutching the bedsheet.
The head resting on a pillow; combine with on side or on back.
A pillow held against the chest or face while lying or sitting.
The body stretches out horizontally, resting its full weight on a flat surface.
The body lies flat with the face turned against or beside the surface.
The figure rests horizontally on a bed, floor, or ground, viewed from the front or side.
Lying on a bed rather than the ground; the bed and bedding are drawn.
Lying on the floor or the ground with no furniture under the body.
Lying along a sofa, often with the legs bent to fit.
Reclining with both arms stretched overhead along the surface, torso elongated.
The figure lies down with both hands raised above the head or lifted in the air.
The figure lies face up with the back against the surface and chest toward the viewer.
The figure lies on one side with legs stacked and an arm pillowing the head.
The figure lies face down with chest and belly pressed against the surface.
The figure rests with eyes closed in peaceful slumber, usually on a pillow or bed.
The figure sleeps with both arms raised loosely above the head on the pillow.
Curls the body tightly on its side with the knees drawn up to the chest and the arms wrapped in close.
Lays the figure on its back with the thighs pressed back toward the chest so the body doubles over on itself.
Lies flat with the arms and legs stretched wide apart, the body spread into an X on the ground.

categories.name: Hand and Arm Poses
categories.description: Terms for arm placement, hand placement, and gesture.

entries.description: One arm lifts high above the shoulder, exposed from armpit to wrist.
Two arms lock hands over a table, each straining to force the other down.
The fingers curl tightly into a balled fist with tense raised knuckles.
Both arms fold over the chest in a firm closed-off posture.
Index and middle fingers form a V held up near the face or chest.
One hand extends to grip another hand in a firm formal greeting.
Two open palms slap together at head height in celebration.
Arms cradle a small infant against the chest, supporting its head and body.
Fingers grip some item in the palm, presenting or examining it.
Fingers lace together loosely or clasp between two linked figures.
Arms strain upward hoisting a barbell or dumbbell with muscles flexed hard.
The figure's own two hands press or fold together in front of the torso.
The hands curl into soft rounded paws held up near the chest in a cute animal manner.
Hands position over a violin, guitar, or other instrument with fingers mid-performance.
An extended index finger aims directly at a person or object.
A fist drives forward with the arm fully extended and the torso twisted behind it.
One hand snaps up beside the brow in a crisp formal military gesture.
A raised fist with the thumb pointing upward in an approving gesture.
Fingers press rapidly across a keyboard with eyes fixed on the screen ahead.
Hands rub together under running water at a sink, often with soap foam.
A hand flutters in a farewell wave, usually with a soft or wistful expression.
An open palm swings side to side in a bright cheerful greeting.
The back of a hand dabs sweat from the brow in relief or exhaustion.
Grabbing an ankle.
An arm laid across another's shoulders.
One arm folds behind the torso, partly hidden, in a reserved formal stance.
Grabbing an arm.
An arm pulled behind the body.
An arm laid on a support.
Weight supported on hands placed on the ground.
An arm folded beneath the chest.
The bare underside of a raised arm shows from the shoulder down to the torso.
Both arms straight up over the head, as in a stretch.
Both arms hanging naturally; standing at attention for a stiffer stance.
Hands behind the back, handy for keeping hands out of view.
Both elbows bent; the arms not hanging straight.
Both arms raised overhead.
Both arms extend fully overhead with fingers spread toward the sky.
Seated with the arms planted behind, leaning back on them.
A beckoning hand, palm up or fingers curling; stays in frame better than reaching.
One elbow bent.
Dark stains on the hands.
The fingers curl into hooked claws held up in a menacing or feral gesture.
A closed fist held rigid with the fingers wrapped hard into the palm.
Fists clenched, often with determined brows.
Pinching or clutching clothing.
Grabbing a collar; somewhat hard.
Covering someone else's eyes.
Arms covering a bare chest, with a shy blush.
Hands over the crotch; in safe content a skirt held down.
Hands over the face, like refusing a photo or shielding from a flash.
Head clutched or shielded with the arms, as in alarm or an earthquake; cowering is the crouched version but unstable.
Fingertips covering the nipples, narrower than covering breasts.
Hands over both ears; without ears in the negative it becomes cupping to listen.
A hand over the own eyes; the one-hand glamour version needs several tries with one hand covering own eyes, seductive smile, hand up.
Cracking the knuckles; unreliable.
Hands cupped as if to hold water.
Clutching a curtain.
A curtsey holding the skirt; clothing turns British as a side effect.
Cleanly drawn fingers, often with an expressive hand gesture; usable as a quality tag.
The clumsy-girl pose, tapping the own head with the tongue out; weak.
Finger guns with both hands.
Grabbing a face.
Fidgeting with the fingers at the chest or a hand at the cheek, with a shy or troubled expression; index fingers together for just the fingertips.
Counting on the fingers, with numbers in the background; too random to be useful.
Fingers forming a framing rectangle; low success, pair with looking through fingers.
An index finger presses vertically against the lips in a quiet thoughtful gesture.
A closed hand; clenched fists is not a tag, so name each fist or use this.
Two characters bumping fists, or one fist held out.
A triumphant fist thrust upward.
Seated or lying with the arms planted in front taking the weight.
Fingers laced before the mouth with glinting eyes; weak alone. Opaque_glasses hides the eyes behind reflecting lenses.
A flying tackle hug, often mid-jump.
One hand closes on something.
Grabbing someone's buttocks.
Tilting someone's chin up with a hand; imminent kiss to imply a kiss.
Grabbing someone's ear.
Grabbing someone's foot.
Grabbing someone's hand; other hand-holding tags are steadier.
A hand takes hold of another figure's head.
Arms take hold of a figure from behind.
A hand grips its own hair.
Guiding another's hand to the own chest.
A finger winds a lock of hair round and round in a flirtatious or nervous habit.
A hand rests in the gap between the thighs while seated.
A hand takes hold of another figure's backside.
A hand closes on a head.
Two characters holding hands.
Fingers rake or rest inside the hair, often in stress or thought.
One hand slips inside a pants or jacket pocket with the arm bent.
A hand raised close to the neck.
A hand laid on someone's cheek.
A hand under another figure's chin.
A hand laid on someone's face.
A hand resting on someone's head; headpat for the petting gesture.
A hand laid on another figure's neck.
A hand laid on another figure's shoulder.
A hand laid on another figure's stomach.
A hand holding or resting on an arm, own or another's.
A hand on another's back.
A hand against the cheek, own or another's.
A hand flat on the chest.
A hand at the chin; thinking or appraising.
A hand touching the face.
A hand planted on the ground taking weight.
A hand resting on the top of the head, own or another's.
A hand grips or tips a hat, hood, or helmet resting on the head.
A hand on a knee.
A hand resting on a leg.
A hand at the back or side of the neck; often sheepish.
A hand on the own buttock, usually gripping.
A hand on the own cheek, close to head rest.
A palm presses flat against the figure's own chest in sincerity or surprise.
Fingers rest beneath the chin or along the jaw in a pondering pose.
A hand cupped to the ear as if asking to repeat.
A hand on the own face, close to head rest.
A hand to the forehead as if checking for fever; often lands on top of the head.
A hand on the own head.
One hand plants firmly on the hip with the elbow jutting outward.
A palm rests flat on the figure's own knee while seated.
A hand laid on one's own neck.
A hand on a shoulder, own or another's.
A hand resting on a thigh.
A single hand rises to about head height with the palm open.
Meant as hands hanging naturally but often breaks; arms at sides is reliable.
Both hands wrap around each other in front of the body.
Both hands tuck into pockets, thumbs often hooked outside the fabric.
Both hands laid on another figure's head.
Both hands laid on another figure's hips.
Both palms press against the chest with fingers spread over the heart.
Both hands rest on the hips with elbows flared wide in a confident stance.
Hands on the knees, often in a knees-up sit.
Hands placed somewhere on the own chest or upper body; random.
Palms together in prayer, or hands joined with another; own hands clasped for the own, holding_hands for another's.
Both hands raised.
A hand takes hold of a head.
A head pat; alone the main character receives it.
Both hands curve together to frame a heart shape in front of the face or chest.
Two characters forming one heart with their hands; use 2girls.
Three characters forming a heart; use 3girls.
The head held in the hands.
The figure holds something.
Gripping someone's wrist; the subject may be the one gripped.
The figure holds an axe.
A book held in the hand.
A bottle held in the hand.
A phone held in the hand.
The figure holds a cigarette.
A box, bag, jar, or other container held.
A cup held in the hand.
The figure holds a dagger.
Food held in the hand.
Holding someone's hand; holding own hand for the own.
The figure holds a head in its hands.
A mug held in the hand.
An unspecified object held; name the object as its own tag beside it.
Holding a phone, usually a smartphone; viewer holding phone puts the phone hand into a first-person frame.
The figure holds a plate.
Holding glasses that have been taken off.
The figure holds a syringe.
The figure holds a tray.
Replace {object} with the item the subject should hold.
A hand taking hold of a horn.
The horns hand sign; may add demon horns and open the hands instead.
Arms wrapped around the own body, close to crossed arms; breast hold may be nearer the intent.
Clinging to someone's leg.
Both arms wrap tightly around a plush toy, pillow, or object against the chest.
The instant before hugging another character.
Arms opened toward the camera for a hug.
One index finger lifts upward in a did-you-know or warning gesture.
Index fingertips touching.
A grandiose theatrical stance; works well but pulls the whole design toward that manga style, and dodododo or menacing (jojo) add sound effects.
A specific character's confident hand-out pose; usually summons that character instead.
A hand taking hold of a leg.
A man's hand on another figure's neck.
A man's hand on another figure's shoulder.
Two characters hugging face to face.
A hand closing on a neck.
Grabbing a necktie; often fails, and neckwear grab covers ascots and the like.
A hand offered for a handshake or holding out an object.
The refined lady laugh with a hand at the mouth; weak.
Thumb and index finger form a circle while the other three fingers extend.
One hand at another figure's throat.
One hand closed on a neck.
An open hand, with a beckoning reach toward the camera as a side effect.
Both arms extend wide open to the sides in a welcoming or pleading gesture.
A hand held out ahead, inviting or rescuing.
The own hands clasped, usually with interlocked fingers; steepled fingers for fingertips together.
Showing the palm; negative palm tree if a tree appears, and unreliable.
The martial-arts fist-in-palm salute; unreliable.
The finger-through-ring gesture; the ring forms but the gesture often fails.
Pointing at someone, or being pointed at.
A thumb or index finger indicates the figure's own chest in surprise or question.
Pointing at the camera with eye contact and foreshortening.
Pointing at the ground.
Pointing ahead.
Pointing sideways; unreliable.
Pointing upward.
Pointing with the thumb raised as well as the index finger.
An index finger to the lips, reading as pensive rather than hushing.
The bunny hands pose, which also adds rabbit ears.
One arm lifted above shoulder height.
Both arms lifted above shoulder height.
A fist raised skyward, sometimes thrust forward instead; fist pump for the triumphant version.
One hand lifted, palm usually forward; a wave, a stop, or a greeting.
An arm stretches toward something beyond the frame with open grasping fingers.
A hand reaching toward the camera.
A shadow-puppet hand, usually the fox; negative shadows if the shadow itself intrudes.
Clutching bedsheets; pair with lying and bed.
A shrug in the western manner, with a comic lean to the drawing.
An index finger held vertically against the lips demands silence.
One hand at another figure's throat.
Both arms opened wide to the sides.
Fingertips from both hands touch to form a pointed arch at chest height.
Hands close around another figure's throat.
Arms closing round another figure's body.
Both hands at another figure's throat.
Both hands take the throat from behind.
A casual two-finger greeting; brings military clothing.
Both hands tucked between the legs, usually in a knees-splayed sit; endearing and reliable.
A victory pose with raised arms, V sign or fist.
A villainous arched-back, arms-wide sneer; mostly makes the subject look villainous.
Both hands raised partway in a cheer, short of a full overhead raise.
Arms crossed in an X; the eyes may turn into X marks, so negative x-shaped_pupils.
Index fingers crossed in an X; the eyes may follow.
Arms held out in a shambling zombie walk; without direction the character turns zombie-like too.
The open inner surface of the hands turned toward the viewer, fingers spread and creases showing.
Both hands reach up to grip or cradle the ears.
Fingertips jammed into both ears to shut out noise, shoulders hunched up.
One fingertip pressed to the rim or bridge of the glasses, nudging them back into place.
Two fingers or a whole hand laid on the glasses, gripping the rim or the temple.
A hand held up with the thumb, index, and little finger extended while the middle and ring fingers fold to the palm.
A raised hand with the index and little fingers up and the middle and ring fingers pinned down by the thumb, the rock horns sign.
Both hands raised beside the head with the index and middle fingers curling twice in the air to mime quotation marks.
A hand held up with all fingertips pinched together and pointing upward, often shaken in exasperation.
Both hands meet so the fingers and thumbs form a ring shape in front of the body, as for a zero or a frame.
The index and middle fingers of one hand hooked over each other in a hopeful or sneaky sign.
Fingers bent inward in a loose curl, neither fully open nor closed into a fist.
A palm shown to the viewer with the thumb tucked in and the four fingers folding down over it, a silent call for help.
Both hands raised with thumb, index, and little finger extended in the same sign, often thrust toward the viewer.
Both hands throw the rock horns at once, index and little fingers up with the thumb holding the middle fingers down.
Both hands form an L with the thumb and index finger extended at a right angle, often held up beside the face.
Both hands held up with four fingers spread straight and the thumb folded across the palm.
Both fists held out with thumbs pointing to the ground in a doubled sign of disapproval.
Both hands raised in a thumbs up, fists closed and both thumbs pointing straight up side by side.
Both hands held up making the two finger V sign, one on each side of the face.
A closed fist with the thumb pushed out between the index and middle fingers.
The hand shaped like a pistol, index finger extended forward and the thumb cocked upward.
One hand with the thumb and index finger crossed into a tiny heart, the other fingers curled down.
One closed fist pressed into the open palm of the other hand in front of the chest.
A hand shaped into a fox head, thumb and two middle fingers pinched into a muzzle with the index and little fingers up as ears.
Both hands held up with every finger bent and flexing, miming a grab at someone.
Thumb and index finger curled into a ring held around the eye like a lens, framing it up close.
A raised hand with the index and middle fingers extended and the ring and little fingers folded to the palm in a blessing.
A hand at the brim, tilting or lifting the hat away from the head in greeting.
Both arms curved up overhead so the hands meet and the arms trace one large heart.
One hand grips an object while that same hand still forms a sign, fingers splayed around what it holds.
The two finger V sign turned around, the back of the hand out and the palm toward the body.
Both hands interlocked to leave a small diamond window between the fingers, with an eye peering through it.
Hands pressed together into ritual finger seals at chest height, as if chanting a spell.
Thumb and index finger held out at a right angle so the hand reads as the letter L.
The middle finger alone thrust upward from a closed fist, back of the hand toward the viewer.
Three middle fingers raised together with the thumb and little finger folded down, reading as a W.
Palm turned upward with thumb and index finger curled into a small coin sized circle.
A flat hand waved in refusal, often both hands crossed in front of the chest to say stop.
Four fingers held up and spread apart with the thumb folded across the palm.
An old formal greeting with the torso bowed, one arm sweeping out low and the other tucked at the waist.
Both hands held open with fingers straight and palms shown, nothing hidden in either.
Thumb and middle finger pinched together with the other fingers curved out like orchid petals.
One fist tapped down into the open palm of the other hand, the gesture of a sudden bright idea.
Thumb and index finger brought almost tip to tip with a narrow gap left between them.
The little finger lifted away from the others in a dainty affected hold.
Thumb and little finger extended from a closed fist and shaken loosely in a surfer greeting.
The ring finger folded down to the palm while the other fingers and the thumb stay extended.
A finger or flat hand dragged sideways across the front of the throat as a silent threat.
Every finger splayed wide apart, each digit clearly separated from the next.
One or both arms thrust forward with the palm flat and the fingers pointing up, blocking the way.
One arm held rigid and raised at an upward angle with the palm down and the fingers straight.
A closed fist with the thumb jabbed downward in flat disapproval.
Both hands brought together with thumbs and index fingers meeting to frame a triangle.
Index and middle fingers raised into a V with the palm out and the rest of the hand closed.
A V of two fingers held up against the face so the eye sits between them.
A V of two fingers held across the lips, the mouth framed between them.
A raised open palm with the fingers parted into two pairs between the middle and ring finger, thumb out.
Three fingers held up and spread, or two fingers with the thumb out, reading as the letter W.
A hand lifted and swept side to side in greeting, sometimes with motion lines trailing it.
A hand raised to the head to straighten or settle a hat or other headwear into place.
Both hands raised to grip or hold the hat being worn, pressing it down onto the head.
A removed hat held against the chest in a solemn respectful gesture.
A hat held in the hand rather than worn, carried at the side or in front of the body.
A helmet carried in the hand or tucked under the arm instead of being worn.
A hand at the throat straightens or tugs a shirt collar or a worn collar into place.
Fingers pinch and straighten the ribbon tied at the collar, resettling its bow.
A hand fixes the knotted neckerchief at the throat, tugging the knot or smoothing its tails, on the wearer or on someone else.
Fingers lift or reposition a necklace at the collarbone, the chain or pendant caught mid adjustment.
A hand grips the knot of a necktie and straightens or loosens it at the throat.
Hands pull a scarf snug around the neck or resettle its wrap, on the wearer or on someone else.
A finger hooks the shirt collar and pulls it slightly down or away from the neck, a flustered or overheated gesture.
Both hands raised to clasp or cradle the own throat, elbows lifted and the face framed between the forearms.
A hand clutches a scarf while it is being worn, tugging or adjusting it at the neck.
Both arms thrown straight up and out in a V of joy, the body forming the shape of the emoticon.
Both arms spread straight out to the sides like wings, usually while running or in motion.
One arm extended straight out and the other drawn back bent at the elbow, the head turned along the extended arm as if aiming a bow.
One arm hangs relaxed at the side of the body while the other arm does something else.
One arm raised and bent so the hand rests behind the head, elbow pointing out.
A rude gesture with one forearm raised bent at the elbow while the other hand slaps or grips the crook of that arm.
An object or a person tucked and carried under one arm, held snug against the side of the torso.
Holds both arms up with the elbows bent and the wrists limp, hands dangling in front of the body like a cartoon ghost.
Sets one arm up behind the head while the other hand rests on the hip, usually with the weight cocked to one side.
Extends one arm straight out away from the body while the other stays lowered or relaxed.
Both hands mirror the same gesture, held at matching heights on either side of the body.
One hand reaches across to rest on the figure's own shoulder, the arm folded over the chest.
Both hands come up to rest on the figure's own shoulders, arms crossed over the chest.
An object carried slung or balanced over one shoulder, steadied there by a raised hand.
A sword laid back across one shoulder, the blade angled up behind the head.
A hand reaching back to clutch the figure's own wing, fingers closed around a feathered or membranous edge.

categories.name: Multi-Subject Poses
categories.description: Terms for contact, arrangement, and interaction among multiple subjects.

entries.description: An adult holds an infant securely against the chest or hip, supporting its head.
An arm around a partner's shoulders.
An arm around a partner's waist.
One figure's arm drapes around the other's shoulders or waist in a loose half embrace.
Two characters with buttocks touching; adult models tend to give a side-by-side rear comparison, so add back-to-back for a true back-to-back.
Carrying someone like a baby; without attributes an actual baby appears.
Two figures stand pressed spine to spine, facing in opposite directions.
Two characters belly to belly; rare and failure-prone.
A chest resting on a carried object; state carrying and the object.
One figure bears another's full weight in the arms while standing or moving.
One figure slings another limply across the shoulders, head hanging down the back.
A cheek resting on another's chest; fails without detailed tags.
An adult supports a child against the hip or chest, holding the legs steady.
A huddle circle; enough people that each breaks, and some models draw a stray circle instead.
Each arm hugged by a different character; pair with girl sandwich.
Kissed on both cheeks by two characters; pair with girl sandwich.
Exactly two characters in frame as the paired focus.
Two figures lock gazes directly, eyes meeting across the space between them.
Two figures stand or sit facing each other at very close range.
A person carried across both shoulders.
A button popping off a strained shirt; unreliable.
Two figures lean in until their foreheads touch, eyes often gently closed.

entries.description: The general existing light of a space, even and low with soft shadowing.

The main light source shaping the subject, strongest from one side.

A narrow light tracing the subject outline, separating it from a dark background.
Circular frontal lighting reflected as ring shaped catchlights in the eyes.
The subject rendered as a dark solid shape against a bright background.
Diffused gentle light with gradual shadow edges and flattering even coverage.
Light dividing the face into a fully lit half and a fully shadowed half.
Light from directly above, deepening the eye sockets and shading under the chin.

The light source behind the subject, edges bright and the face in shade.
A flattering, glowing light on the subject that tends toward backlighting.
The body glows like a jellyfish; unstable.
Soft bleed of bright areas into neighbors.
Radiating light rays from the source, leaning toward backlighting.

Visible shafts of light through air.

Low, directional light with heavy shadow and a sombre tone.
Cool pale blue moonlight washing the scene with gentle silver tones.

A character explanation sheet with a main figure surrounded by text and face variations; highly random.
Several illustrations pasted together on one canvas; highly random.
Several bordered character panels of equal size lined up in a row or column, a group-picture format.
Book or magazine cover styling; magazine cover or dojin cover sharpens it.
Body-pillow art: a character lying on sheets with a suggestive expression; pairs with on back, bed sheet, lying.
Dust and fragments hanging in the air for a tense atmosphere; dust cloud for smoke-like haze.
A cloud of dust, including the comic scuffle cloud.
A framed expression-challenge grid of front-facing faces; more usable than expressions.
A set of the same character's expressions; on illustrious-family models it floods the canvas.
App-style doodles on the face; weak, use drawn tags instead.
A phone camera screen with black bars and a shutter button; use a portrait canvas and negative phone if a handset appears.
A photo-like picture, often with a white polaroid border or placed on a desk, and a snapshot pose; pushes the subject toward photorealism.
A game, stream, or phone capture look with floating, unreadable text.
A collectible figure appears, often the character rendered as one or a figure inside the scene; a character on a cut-out scenery base is faux_figurine.
Diving underwater without equipment; specify pose and placement.
A group picture of three or more characters.
A two-panel before-and-after adult comic format; needs a landscape canvas and adult tags to land.
A sitting pose with nothing drawn under the character.
A leaning pose with no wall drawn; low success on illustrious-family models.
An isometric illustration of buildings or a town seen from diagonally above with the character in it; diorama for a cut-out scene, dollhouse view for a room plan.
Reads as collage rather than a magazine page: cut-and-paste assembled illustrations.
Magazine-cover layout with unreadable text; watch for invented titles resembling real magazines.
A phone selfie in a mirror; the character may spill past the mirror edge, so pair with holding phone and reflection focus.
A mosaic-tiled background rather than a mosaic of the whole picture.
A motion-filled shot similar to 1ms shutter speed; no effect on illustrious-family models.
A striking, designed movie-poster layout.
The camera half submerged, showing above and below the waterline at once; may sink entirely, so steer with canvas size, sky, or cowboy shot.
A physical photograph inside the picture, hung on a wall or held.
A frame around the whole picture, or a framed picture hanging on a background wall.
Instant-photo styling with a wide white bottom border; white border strengthens it, and negative character signature or text if a signature appears.
Photo-booth sticker styling; weak, and drawn doodles come better from drawn tags.
Rubble on the ground; ruins for a ruined building.
The character seen in a mirror looking back at the viewer; may spill past the mirror edge.
Feet dipped in water, usually barefoot.
Part of the body in water, as in a hot spring; alone it may submerge everything, so specify pose and placement.
A standing character illustration, usually a natural front-facing full figure; can drift toward game character art and is somewhat unstable.
A photo being taken, with the character posing for the camera; negative viewfinder or fake phone screenshot if a capture overlay appears.

entries.term: three views from front back and side
entries.description: The same character drawn from three directions.
On a portrait canvas, a trading-card layout with frame and rank marks; negative card (medium) if physical playing cards appear.
A camera viewfinder overlay with battery and REC marks.
A four-panel vertical comic strip. In a negative it removes panel layouts and gutters.
A decorated border drawn around the whole image, as on a framed print or an old portrait.
A lace pattern running along the edges of the image as a frame.
A composition mirrored across a central axis; faces, poses, and backgrounds line up left and right.
Yields a head to toe outfit showcase, the figure posed to display a coordinated on-trend ensemble.
A grid of thirty five small portraits of one character, each head carrying a different expression.
A sheet of one character repeated through a set of twelve expressions, from blank and smiling to crying.

entries.term: hurt expressions of your wife practice
entries.description: A sheet of one character repeated through a range of hurt, pained and tearful expressions.
The same character repeated in several small portraits, each one carrying a different expression.
A sheet of one character repeated through a set of mildly lewd, flushed and teasing expressions.
A single self-contained comic panel with a border, holding the whole gag or scene in one frame with a caption or balloon.
A comic strip of three bordered panels in a continuous vertical or horizontal run, reading a short scene in three beats.
A comic strip of five bordered panels in a continuous vertical or horizontal run, reading a short scene in five beats.
Frames the picture as square music cover art with an artist name and title laid over the image and a clean square edge.
A glossy commercial photo card portrait of a performer, posed and lit like a studio publicity photo, in a collectible print.
Lays the picture out as a calendar page, with a month name and a grid of dates printed beside or beneath the artwork.
Frames the picture as a music CD cover devoted to one character, with the character large and a song title and name over the art.
Arranges the picture as an organized grid or lineup of labeled figures or panels for side by side comparison.
Frames the picture as the front cover of a book or magazine, with a title, author name, and other printed text over the art.
Inserts a smaller picture, often a face or a pair of eyes in close-up, cutting across the main image inside its own framed strip.
Lays out symbols, arrows, and short labels to show a flow of steps or connections, such as a relationship map.
A miniature scene enclosed in a box or set on a small cut-out base, with props building a partial background around the figures.
Frames the picture as the cover of a self-published comic, with a title, a circle name, and a content rating over the art.
Frames the picture as a home video sleeve, with a title, a spine, and a disc logo laid over the art in a tall rectangle.
Edges the picture with a border that dissolves gradually into the image instead of stopping at a hard line.
Frames the picture as a mock-up magazine, comic, album, or game cover, with invented titles and blurbs laid over the art.
Adds a drawn vertical scrollbar along the edge, suggesting the picture continues below the visible area.
Restages a famous painting's composition and palette with the characters swapped in, mimicking the classical or modern original.
Renders the picture as a video game screen capture, with health bars, menus, dialogue boxes, or other interface overlaid.
A small simplified square image of a program or file, flat and bold with a rounded frame, as it appears on a desktop or taskbar.
A picture captioned with bold white block capitals outlined in black at the top and bottom, in the classic internet meme layout.
A thin one or two line border drawn inside the picture, clearly set in from the outer edge as a frame within the frame.
Adds black bars across the top and bottom of the picture, narrowing it to a wide cinematic strip.
Frames the picture as the cover of a manga volume, with a large title logo, author name, and volume number over the art.
Lays out a fighting-game style sheet of one character repeated in several attack poses, each with a label or input notation beside it.
Puts two or more four-panel vertical comic strips side by side in one picture, each strip a separate short gag read top to bottom.
Divides the picture into several sections, each rendered entirely in a single different hue, so the parts read as tinted panels next to each other.
Yields a polished promotional wallpaper layout: characters posed against a wide clean background with open space left for a logo and desktop icons.
Adds a small bonus strip or side illustration beside or after the main piece, drawn looser and more casual than the work it accompanies.
Lets a character or object spill over the frame, letterbox bars, or panel edge that contains the rest of the picture, breaking out of the border.
A drawn character cut out of paper and photographed propped up in a real-world setting, its flat cartoon surface contrasting with the photo around it.
Lays the picture out as a small credit-card sized collectible card, with the illustration filling the card face beside a value mark or logo strip.
Puts solid vertical bars down the left and right sides of the picture, leaving a narrower upright image in the center.
Sets two contrasting elements against each other in the picture, such as light and dark halves, opposing colors, or characters from rival sides.
Makes the entire picture read as a printed poster, with a bold central image, title lettering, credits, and a designed layout with margins.
Lays out a top-down diagram of a room's desks or seats with a name or small face on each, showing who sits where.
Lays the picture out as a printed pencil board: a glossy rounded-corner rectangle carrying promotional character art edge to edge.
Splits the picture into gallery-style tiles with straight dividing lines or a four-point sparkle shape at the center, mimicking how stitched images sit in an online gallery grid.
Surrounds the subject with caption boxes of measurements, numbers, and labeled traits, like a character profile or data sheet.
Places two nearly identical side-by-side views of the same scene so they merge into a single image with depth when the eyes cross or relax.
Yields an extremely tall narrow picture, at least four times higher than wide, suited to a full standing figure or a stacked vertical scene.
Splits one cohesive picture into several separate images that only reassemble into the whole when tiled together as gallery thumbnails.
Adds thin crop marks at the four corners of the picture, short paired lines showing where a printed sheet would be cut to size.
Divides the picture into three upright panels set side by side, usually a larger central panel flanked by two narrower wings.
Lays the picture out to fit a round paddle fan, with the artwork shaped to the fan face and a handle or fastener hole cutting into the bottom edge.
Shows the same character repeated several times across the picture in different outfits, hairstyles, or color schemes for comparison.
Lays the picture out as game box art with a bold title logo, a platform banner, a rating badge, and a dramatic hero image.
Yields an extremely wide panoramic strip, at least four times wider than tall, suited to sweeping landscapes or a row of characters.
Frames the picture in a wide 16:9 or similar aspect ratio, like a modern monitor or film frame, with a broad horizontal field.
A single illustration laid out as an episode closing card, with a short caption or preview line and a staff credit in the corner.
A chapter-opening hero illustration with the title and a tagline laid over a striking full-page image of the lead character.
Lays out the stages of a drawing side by side, from rough sketch through lineart and flat color to the finished piece.
Polished key-visual artwork with the cast arranged in a showcase composition, a clean high-finish render, and often a title logo or blank space left for one.
Frames the picture as a screen capture, with a browser, app or video player interface, window edges and a cursor or status bar around the content.
Joins several separate pictures edge to edge into one taller or wider image, the artwork continuing across the joins.
Yields the clean version of an illustration with all dialogue, titles, logos and rating marks removed, leaving only the artwork.

categories.name: Content Rating
categories.description: Rating vocabulary that sets the content tier of a picture, usable in the positive or the negative.

entries.description: The explicit rating: genitals, penetration, ejaculation, and cut-ins become far more likely than with nsfw; negative penis or trembling when unwanted.
The all-ages rating; in the positive it removes adult mood, in the negative it strengthens it.
The mild adult rating; nipples begin to appear.
The all-ages rating in its colon form, which is part of the tag.
The mild adult rating in its colon form.
The sensitive rating in its colon form.
The sensitive rating: some exposure, nothing further.

categories.name: Visual registers
categories.description: Whole-look presets a series or a shot can adopt: each names the coverage scale, camera behaviour, light, colour, pacing, and finish that make a picture read as that kind of film, and the words that evoke it. Name the behaviour, not only the label; a label alone leaves the choices to the model.

entries.description: Shapes, colour, texture, and movement express the feeling without a story: macro detail, light play, particles, reflections, slow and rhythmic motion.

High-energy sequence cut to the theme: character run-ins, speed lines and impact flashes, dramatic cuts between scenes, poses held at peak tension, strong backlight and lens flare, a title card. One beat per clip.

Quiet observational anime: medium shots on a soft 35mm feel, tiny secondary motion (a sleeve in the wind, a snack bag crinkling), hand-painted sky gradients, warm rim light against cool shadow. Avoid action poses and glossy 3D.
Warm natural window light, cheerful pastel colour, medium-wide 28mm feel at eye level, simple motion gags. Avoid slapstick chaos, distortion, and dark dramatic lighting.

Film-like coverage: medium to close shots, one wide establishing shot per scene, camera moves motivated by action or a look, shallow focus, directional light with a colour grade. Write the behaviour (slow push-in, warm practical light, teal and orange grade) rather than the word alone, which leaves every choice to the model.
Close medium hero composition, slow luxury camera language (a slow arc, light sliding across a surface), soft edge light, material texture named. Avoid floating renders and sterile white backgrounds.

Observational look: shoulder-height handheld feel, slightly imperfect framing, natural fluorescent or window light, tactile ordinary motion (steam moves, a bowl is set down), honest and unposed. Avoid dramatic spotlights, product gloss, and fake film grain.
Typography carries the song: words appear on or beside the picture in time with the vocal, over simple animated backgrounds or slow abstract motion.

The page as film: variable panel sizes as shot sizes, a double-page spread as the wide shot, dramatic close-ups on faces, high-contrast black and white, screentone, speed and focus lines, impact frames, borderless panels for atmosphere.

A short story cut to the music: cinematic coverage of a beat that gives each scene a reason to exist, cutaways and B-roll for texture, colour keyed to the mood (warm gold, cold blue shadows, neon glow, or plain daylight).

The artist performs to camera: lip sync, direct address, cuts on the beat, whip pans and crash zooms, strobe or colour-wash lighting, slow motion on the chorus, wide then close alternation. The song's energy sets the camera speed.
Neutral eye-level coverage, available light, no grade beyond a slight warmth, motion only from the subjects; the register for evidence stills and continuity plates.
Clean 1970s future design, warm sunlight with a soft cyan glow, wide 35mm feel with a smooth slow push-in, hopeful mood. Avoid neon cyberpunk and dark dystopia.
Medium-wide 40mm feel, quiet symmetrical composition, warm practical light against soft blue street colour, tiny emotional changes (a look up, a step closer). Avoid posed romance and melodrama.
Cuts the piece like a music video: a performer or subject framed in rhythmic stylized shots, dramatic colored lighting, and quick changes of set and mood.

categories.name: Camera movement
categories.description: Moves of the camera body or lens for video prompts. Pair every move with a speed word or a duration, because models have no default speed; describe what each stage of a move reveals rather than stacking verbs; one move per shot is what most surfaces honour.

entries.description: The camera travels a curved path around the subject without completing a circle; subtle added motion.
The camera lifts high above the scene; establishing scale. Also drone rise.
An extremely fast zoom in or out; comedy and shock reveals.
The camera body moves closer; the background shifts in perspective. Also written push-in. Use for tension and emotion.
The camera body retreats; the environment expands around the subject. Also written pull-back or pull out. Use for reveals and endings.
The body dollies while the lens zooms the opposite way, so the subject holds size while the background stretches; vertigo.
Electronically stabilised motion, the smoothest, for complex paths.
Subtle natural shake and slightly imperfect framing; documentary realism.

The camera does not move at all. Reinforce it in prose (the camera is entirely motionless for the duration) and give the scene other motion, because a static frame is the hardest request for a video model.
The camera circles the subject completely; hero moments. Works on some surfaces only.
The camera swivels horizontally on a fixed position, without parallax; follows action or reveals what is beside the frame.
The camera swivels horizontally to the right on a fixed position.
The whole camera drops straight down.
The whole camera rises straight up.
Same as dolly out: the body travels backward.
Same as dolly in: the body travels forward, keeping perspective natural (a zoom does not).
The camera and framing hold while the focus shifts between planes; the cheapest way to redirect attention mid-shot.
Time slowed; the action plays at a fraction of its speed. Write which action is slowed and for how long.
A word such as slow, gentle, or fast, or a duration such as a five-second pan, attached to a camera move; without one the speed is arbitrary.
Stabilised handheld: smooth while walking, following without rawness.
The camera pivots vertically downward on a fixed position.
The camera pivots vertically upward on a fixed position; reveals height.
The camera follows a moving subject, keeping it in frame; name the direction it follows from.
The camera slides sideways to the left, parallel to the subject; walk-and-talks.
The camera slides sideways to the right, parallel to the subject.
A very fast pan that smears the frame into motion blur; an energetic transition between two views.
The lens focal length increases; the image flattens and the framing tightens without the body moving.
The lens focal length decreases; the framing widens without the body moving.

categories.name: Shot grammar
categories.description: The units and rules of coverage: what kind of shot a frame is within a scene, and the continuity rules between shots. These are planning words; most become framing terms or camera moves in the prompt itself.

entries.description: Keep the camera on one side of the axis between two characters so each stays on the same side of the frame across cuts; crossing it flips left and right.
The imaginary line between two interacting characters, or along a character's movement, that the 180-degree rule protects.
A contemplative pause with no camera or subject movement; a beat held before or after an action.
The set of shots gathered so a scene can be edited coherently: master, singles, over-the-shoulders, inserts, reactions.
An interruption of the main action with a view of something else, followed by a cut back.
Foreground, middle, and background all sharp.
A cut from a character looking to what they are looking at; the audience reads the second shot as what the first one sees.
A doorway, window, or arch inside the picture frames the subject.
A shot of part of the scene from a different angle or focal length than the master, emphasising a detail (hands, an object) already covered.
One shot that holds the whole dramatised scene from start to finish with every player in view; the geography the closer shots inherit.
A cut that joins two shots on a shared shape, motion, or position so the transition reads as one gesture.
A move that follows a character's action or look rather than moving on its own; the reason for the move is visible in the frame.
A single narrative moment per short clip; a second beat in the same clip competes with the first.
A cutaway to a participant reacting to what has just happened.
A shot from the opposite side of the previous one along the same axis; fixtures that were on the right stand on the left.
A narrow plane in focus and the rest soft.
A shot holding one person alone in a scene with others.
A shot holding two people; the distance between them is the content.

categories.name: Manga cinematics
categories.description: Devices from the manga page that image models draw as content: motion and emphasis marks, panel rhythm, and the page's equivalents of shot sizes.

entries.description: A panel without a frame, often full-bleed; signals an open or atmospheric moment and changes the page rhythm.
One image across two facing pages; the manga equivalent of the wide shot.
A tight panel on a face or object to carry an emotional state or an important detail.
Lines radiating from a point to concentrate attention on it; also used for shock and emphasis.
A single bright element against deep black, or near-monochrome darkness with one bright accent.
A single high-contrast frame at the moment of impact, often black and white with radiating lines.
Dense cross-hatching used for shadow, texture, and tension in inked manga.
Panel size as pacing: small regular panels for fast dialogue, a large panel or spread for an emotional or action peak.
Comic panels separated by plain gaps of empty space rather than drawn frame lines, giving the page an open airy layout.
A comic page whose panels and speech balloons read left to right, the reverse of the usual right to left manga order.
Orders the comic panels and speech balloons from right to left across the page, so the reading path runs opposite to a Western strip.
